      "title": "User makes themselves an admin by adding a role field to the profile update",
      "scenario": "A signed-in user calls the profile update endpoint to change their display name, but adds \"role\":\"admin\" to the same JSON body. The handler copies every field onto the user record, so the role is persisted without any check that the caller may set it. The attacker gains administrative privileges over the system with a single request.",
      "component": "PATCH /users/{id} update handler",
      "likelihood": 5,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "takeover" },

        { "quote": "copies every field onto the user record, including fields like role and accountStatus" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-915", "CWE-269"],
      "plainLanguage": "A normal user can sneak \"role: admin\" into the form that changes their name, and the system believes it.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Only allow display-name fields on the user update endpoint",
        "given": "a signed-in user calls PATCH /users/{id}",
        "when": "the JSON body contains fields such as role that the user is not permitted to set",
        "then": "the server binds only an explicit allow-list of self-editable fields and rejects or ignores the privileged fields, leaving role unchanged"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Tampering",
      "title": "Account status can be changed through the profile update, bypassing suspension",
      "scenario": "A user who has been suspended or locked out sends a profile update containing \"accountStatus\":\"active\" and the handler writes it onto the user record, restoring their access. The same field can be set to a disabled value to lock out a victim, denying them service.",
      "component": "PATCH /users/{id} update handler",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "integrity" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "including fields like role and accountStatus" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-915"],
      "plainLanguage": "A banned user can un-ban themselves, or disable someone else's account, using the same name-change request.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Account status is only changed by an administrative flow",
        "given": "a profile update request that includes accountStatus",
        "when": "the caller is the account owner rather than an authorised administrator",
        "then": "the accountStatus value is rejected and the stored status is unchanged"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "No ownership check on the id in the path, so one user can edit another user's record",
      "scenario": "The design states only that the endpoint accepts an id in the path and copies the body onto the user record; no check that the id belongs to the caller is described. A signed-in user iterates ids and updates other people's records, including their role and accountStatus, taking over privileged accounts or defacing profiles across the whole user base.",
      "component": "PATCH /users/{id} authorization",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "low", "reach": "all", "harm": "takeover" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "PATCH /users/{id} accepts a JSON body and copies every field onto the user record" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-639", "CWE-862"],
      "plainLanguage": "Change the user number in the web address and you are editing somebody else's account.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Enforce ownership on the user update endpoint",
        "given": "a signed-in user calls PATCH /users/{id}",
        "when": "the id in the path is not the caller's own user id and the caller has no administrative permission",
        "then": "the request is denied with an authorization error and no field is written"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Spoofing",
      "title": "Identity fields such as email can be overwritten, enabling account takeover by password reset",
      "scenario": "Because every field in the body is copied onto the user record, an attacker who can reach the endpoint for a target record sets the login identifier (for example email) to an address they control, then triggers a password reset and signs in as that user. Verification of the new address is never performed because the field is written directly.",
      "component": "User record store",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "medium", "reach": "many", "harm": "takeover" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "copies every field onto the user record" }
      ],
      "asvs": [],
      "cwe": ["CWE-915", "CWE-640"],
      "plainLanguage": "Someone could change the email on an account and then use \"forgot password\" to walk in.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Identity fields require a verification step",
        "given": "a user update request that changes an identity field such as email or phone",
        "when": "the handler processes the body",
        "then": "the change is held as pending until the new value is verified, and the existing login identifier stays in force until then"
      }
    }
  ]
}
